title: Joint injectivity of fpqc units at every etale object
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\{g_i:T_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], $F$ a sheaf of sets on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets, def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $V\to S$ an étale object. For $t,t'\in F(V)$, suppose the inverse-image adjunction units satisfy $\eta_{g_i,V}(t)=\eta_{g_i,V}(t')$ in $(g_i^{-1}F)(V\times_S T_i)$ for every $i$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units, def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $t=t'$. No compatible datum or local-existence hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tags 03Q1 (3) and 03PU, germ comparison and separatedness; Tag 09XN, uniqueness

proof.text: Base change the fpqc covering to V. For each point v of V, joint surjectivity gives a point y in some T_i times_S V above it. The algebraic closure of the residue field of y supplies a geometric lift r, whose projections to T_i and V give a pointed neighborhood of its image in S.

Apply the germ formula of the inverse-image stalk comparison to t and t′ and the projection of r to T_i. Their equal unit images give equal germs, hence their original germs at the pointed neighborhood V agree.

The pointed-neighborhood filtered-colimit equality criterion yields W -> V with equal restrictions and a geometric lift above v. Choose one for every v. The W cover V, so sheaf separatedness gives t=t′. The empty family handles empty V.
